# harness: the benchmark extension for the resident bundles

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_readme.py from the harness code. Do not edit by hand;
     edit the source the section names and run `python3 scripts/gen_readme.py`. -->

Runs inference and evaluation over the task bundles with [Harbor](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor) **0.24.0**. Each bundle is self-contained: its `task.toml` declares the network policy of every phase and where its verifier runs, and its own `tests/` score the run. The harness adds the agent under test, a model route on the host, and the bookkeeping around a run. It carries no grader, no judge and no network proxy of its own.

## What the bundle owns, and what the harness adds

| Concern | Owner | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Scoring | bundle | `tests/` run by harbor in the verifier environment; the reshaper publishes `verifier/reward.json` as written and never recomputes it |
| Verifier environment | bundle | `[verifier] environment_mode` (`separate`: built from `[verifier.environment].docker_image`, else `tests/Dockerfile`, else `[environment]`) |
| Network policy | bundle | `network_mode` in `[environment]`, `[agent]`, `[verifier]`, enforced by harbor's docker egress-control sidecar, which refuses a trial it cannot enforce |
| Model route | harness | a bridge on the host, passed to harbor as `--allow-agent-host` |
| Agent under test | harness | `tools/openhands_agent` (default) or harbor's `claude-code` |
| Agent-side egress layers | harness | `--disallowedTools` and a PreToolUse guard, only when the task closes its agent phase; the internet audit afterwards |

Trial-level `--extra-docker-compose` and `--mounts` reach the agent environment only, so nothing the harness adds touches a separate verifier.

## Entry points

Registered in `pyproject.toml` under `[project.scripts]` and locked in `uv.lock`:

| Script | Target |
|---|---|
| `harness-infer` | `tools.cli:infer` |
| `harness-eval` | `tools.cli:evaluate` |

```text
    harness-infer [--stage STAGE] <task-dir>       run the agent on one bundle
    harness-eval <trial-dir> <task-dir> [-- ...]   score a recorded rollout
```

Inference is `scripts/run_task.sh`. Evaluation is `harbor trial regrade --task-path <bundle>`: it seeds a new trial with the recorded agent logs and artifacts and runs the bundle's own `tests/` in a separate verifier environment, leaving the source trial untouched. Harbor refuses to regrade a task whose verifier is in shared mode.

## Harbor

Pinned at **0.24.0** in `scripts/lib/harbor.sh` and installed from `scripts/lib/harbor-requirements.lock` (92 packages, every file hash-checked with `--require-hashes`):

```bash
make install-harbor          # bash scripts/lib/harbor.sh install
```

`scripts/patch_harbor.py` runs before every harbor stage. It refuses any harbor other than the pin, applies each patch or reports it as a MISS and exits 1, and is idempotent. Patches applied:

- thinking flag
- fallback_model removal
- ARG_MAX instruction file
- egress sidecar read timeout
- egress sidecar service-name aliases

Behaviour it requires harbor to provide natively (checked, never patched):

- ClaudeCode classifies failures from terminal stream events
- rate_limit_event telemetry is filtered out of classification
- install() skips the network when claude is pre-baked

## Running a task

From `scripts/run_task.sh`:

```text
Run one mcp-atlas Harbor task end-to-end and emit the per-task output/ tree
(same layout complex-mcp's --layout harbor writer produces).

  scripts/run_task.sh tasks/xenon-atomic-cube                 # openhands + opus-5 (defaults)
  AGENT=claude-code scripts/run_task.sh tasks/foo             # harbor's claude-code agent
  CC_MODE=zbridge N=3 scripts/run_task.sh tasks/foo           # openhands on GLM-5.3 (zbridge)
  CC_MODE=bedrock MODEL=claude-opus-5 scripts/run_task.sh tasks/foo  # openhands on AWS Bedrock
  CC_MODE=kiro KIRO_MODEL=claude-opus-5 KIRO_JUDGE_MODEL=gpt-5.6-sol \
      scripts/run_task.sh tasks/foo                           # openhands on Kiro (dynamic model + judge)
  AGENT=oracle scripts/run_task.sh tasks/foo                  # oracle gate
  COPY_TO=/some/dir scripts/run_task.sh tasks/foo           # optional extra mirror

  scripts/run_task.sh --stage reshape tasks/foo               # one stage only

The default agent is OpenHands (tools/openhands_agent). CC_MODE picks the
model route and, where the route exposes a second key, also the judge wire
that the bundle's rubric runs against:

  unset (default) ccbridge -> host's Claude subscription (OAuth). Agent only;
                  judge takes CALLER_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
                  from .env) direct to api.anthropic.com.
  CC_MODE=zbridge zbridge on :8766 -> GLM for the agent. Judge wire unchanged
                  (same ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -> api.anthropic.com path).
  CC_MODE=bedrock no host bridge; the agent calls AWS Bedrock directly from
                  the container with AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK and AWS_REGION
                  forwarded in. The judge also runs on Bedrock in-process via
                  litellm.acompletion against JUDGE_MODEL (BEDROCK_MODEL_IDS
                  alias) using the same AWS creds.
  CC_MODE=kiro    kiro_bridge on 127.0.0.1 (ephemeral port) exposes two keys:
                  agent_key pinned to KIRO_MODEL, judge_key pinned to
                  KIRO_JUDGE_MODEL. Both sides hit kiro-cli; agent and judge
                  models can be set independently per run.

See tools/openhands_agent/README.md and tools/bridges/<mode>/README.md.

Env overrides: AGENT (openhands) MODEL (claude-opus-5) N (1) JOB (<task slug>)
               OUTPUT_DIR (<repo>/output) COPY_TO (unset) BUILD_MULT (3) AT (auto)
               STAGE (all) RUN_OFFSET (auto) SETUP_MULT (6)
               DISALLOWED_TOOLS (WebSearch,WebFetch)
               CC_MODE (unset -> ccbridge on Claude subscription;
                        "zbridge" -> glm-5.3 via :8766;
                        "bedrock" -> AWS Bedrock direct, no host bridge;
                        "kiro"    -> kiro_bridge, two-key agent+judge split)
  bedrock:     AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK (required) BEDROCK_AWS_REGION (required)
               BEDROCK_MODEL_IDS (alias1=id1,alias2=id2 map, resolves MODEL
               and JUDGE_MODEL to full Bedrock inference-profile ARNs)
               JUDGE_MODEL (defaults to MODEL; alias from BEDROCK_MODEL_IDS)
               JUDGE_MODE (bedrock | kiro | anthropic | openai; selects the
               judge wire independently of the agent. default: bedrock)
                 JUDGE_MODE=kiro      needs kiro-cli login + KIRO_JUDGE_MODEL
                 JUDGE_MODE=anthropic needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (direct call)
                 JUDGE_MODE=openai    needs OPENAI_API_KEY (direct call)
               AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY (optional, enables
               the pre-flight bedrock:ListFoundationModels credential check;
               set BEDROCK_CHECK_OFF=1 to skip)
               CC_BRIDGE_ENABLED (0)
               AGENT_HEADROOM_ENABLED (false)
  kiro:        KIRO_MODEL (default: $MODEL; pinned on the agent key)
               KIRO_JUDGE_MODEL (default: $MODEL; pinned on the judge key,
               injected into the verifier as JUDGE_MODEL via --ve)
               KIRO_BRIDGE_START_TIMEOUT_SEC (60) JUDGE_WIRE (anthropic)
               kiro-cli must be logged in on the host; the bridge mints a
               per-run agent_key and judge_key and tears both down at exit.
  judge:       ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (ccbridge/zbridge: the key the rubric judge
               calls api.anthropic.com with; auto-set for bedrock/kiro by
               this script)
               JUDGE_MODEL (bedrock/kiro: which model the judge runs on;
               defaults to the agent MODEL when unset)
               JUDGE_WIRE (anthropic|openai; kiro default anthropic)
  openhands:   CCBRIDGE_SHARED (0: a ccbridge per run, on a free port, stopped
               at exit; 1: one long-lived bridge on CCBRIDGE_PORT (8765) with
               CCBRIDGE_SECRET or tools/bridges/ccbridge/.bridge_secret)
               CCBRIDGE_HOST (127.0.0.1 on macOS when every phase is public,
               else 0.0.0.0, gated by the bridge's secret)
               OPENHANDS_MAX_ITERATIONS (500) OPENHANDS_MAX_CONTINUATIONS (6)
               OPENHANDS_REASONING_EFFORT (SDK default) OPENHANDS_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS (32000)
               OPENHANDS_THINKING_DISPLAY (summarized | omitted)
               OPENHANDS_NUM_RETRIES (5 attempts per model call, backing off 8-64s)

Values may also come from <repo>/.env, which is read as DEFAULTS only: anything
already in the environment wins over it.

Scoring and network policy belong to the bundle, not to this script. Harbor
runs the bundle's own tests/ in the verifier environment its task.toml
declares ([verifier] environment_mode = "separate"), and enforces each phase's
declared network_mode ([environment], [agent], [verifier]) with its docker
egress-control sidecar, refusing a trial whose policy it cannot enforce. This
script adds no grader, no judge and no proxy of its own; the only network
input it makes is --allow-agent-host for its own model bridge on the host.

Stages. The default STAGE=all runs the four below in order, which is the
original one-shot behaviour. They are separable because their costs differ by
orders of magnitude: the agent phase takes minutes and real money, reshaping
takes seconds, and reporting is one HTTP call. A crash between them must not
re-run the agent, so scripts/run_batch.py drives them one at a time and
checkpoints in between.

  preflight  auth, docker, image build/pull               (idempotent)
  harbor     harbor run -> output/<job>/                  (NOT idempotent: makes a trial)
  reshape    harbor_to_output.py -> trajectory/Run_N/      (idempotent)
  finance    finance_reporter.py -> Odoo                  (NOT idempotent: external POST)
  mask       make_delivery.py --mask-only -> strips host   (idempotent; runs
             paths; automatic at the end of reshape + finance)

State that crosses a stage boundary (which Run_N this invocation owns, where
earlier runs were stashed) is written to output/<job>/.run_state.json so a
later stage in a separate process can pick it up.
```

Stages: `all`, `preflight`, `harbor`, `reshape`, `finance`, `mask`. `scripts/run_batch.py` drives them one at a time with a checkpoint between each.

Before the agent phase, `tools/network/preflight_network.py` resolves the task's network plan and verifier environment through harbor's own code and refuses what harbor would refuse after the image build.

## Mode details

`CC_MODE` picks both the agent model route and the judge wire. The default is ccbridge; every mode runs the same OpenHands agent and the same bundle verifier, only the transport changes.

### Default (ccbridge)

- **Agent**: OpenHands → ccbridge on 127.0.0.1 (per-run, ephemeral port) → host's Claude subscription (OAuth, from `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`).
- **Judge**: direct `api.anthropic.com` with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from `.env` or the caller's environment. The bridge is agent-only.
- **Judge model**: whatever the bundle's rubric defaults to (usually `claude-sonnet-5`); override by exporting `JUDGE_MODEL`.

```bash
# .env
CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=sk-ant-oat...
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-api03-...   # judge

scripts/run_task.sh tasks/<slug>
```

### `CC_MODE=zbridge`

- **Agent**: OpenHands → zbridge on `:8766` → GLM-5.3.
- **Judge**: unchanged from the default (direct `api.anthropic.com` with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`).

```bash
CC_MODE=zbridge scripts/run_task.sh tasks/<slug>
```

### `CC_MODE=bedrock`

Both agent and judge call AWS Bedrock directly. No host bridge, no kiro, no Anthropic.

- **Agent**: OpenHands SDK → `litellm.completion` with `bedrock/<model>` prefix. The alias in `MODEL` is resolved to the full inference-profile ARN at call-time via a monkey-patch, so trajectory logs show `claude-opus-5`, not the ARN.
- **Judge**: in-process `litellm.acompletion` from `services/scoring/score_claims.py` and `services/diagnostics/single_model_diagnostic.py`, same alias→ARN resolver, same AWS creds.

```bash
# .env
CC_MODE=bedrock
MODEL=claude-opus-5                            # agent alias
JUDGE_MODEL=gpt-5.6-sol                        # judge alias (defaults to MODEL)
AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK=bedrock-api-key-...
BEDROCK_AWS_REGION=ap-south-1
BEDROCK_MODEL_IDS=claude-opus-5=arn:aws:bedrock:ap-south-1:XXXX:application-inference-profile/XXXX,gpt-5.6-sol=arn:aws:bedrock:ap-south-1:XXXX:application-inference-profile/YYYY

# optional, enables the pre-flight bedrock:ListFoundationModels check
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIA...
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=...
# BEDROCK_CHECK_OFF=1   # set to skip the pre-flight check

scripts/run_task.sh tasks/<slug>
```

Three guards fire before the agent phase:
1. `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` + `BEDROCK_AWS_REGION` must be set, else the run is refused.
2. `MODEL` and `JUDGE_MODEL` must resolve through `BEDROCK_MODEL_IDS`, else the run is refused with the list of known aliases.
3. If `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` is set, a `bedrock:ListFoundationModels` ping validates the creds at startup instead of 20 minutes into the trial.

#### Picking a different judge wire with `JUDGE_MODE`

`CC_MODE=bedrock` locks the agent to Bedrock, but the judge wire is independent. Set `JUDGE_MODE` to compare judge models across runs without changing the agent:

| `JUDGE_MODE` | Judge wire | Env vars needed | Pre-flight check |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bedrock` (default) | AWS Bedrock Converse via `boto3` | existing `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` + `BEDROCK_MODEL_IDS` | strong: SigV4 live ping + ARN resolution |
| `kiro` | kiro-cli through the vendored kiro_bridge | `kiro-cli login` on host + `KIRO_JUDGE_MODEL` | medium: Python import + bridge start |
| `anthropic` | direct `api.anthropic.com` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` + optional `JUDGE_MODEL` | weak: env var existence |
| `openai` | direct `api.openai.com` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` + optional `JUDGE_MODEL` | weak: env var existence |

```bash
# agent on Bedrock, judge on kiro (gpt-5.6-sol)
CC_MODE=bedrock JUDGE_MODE=kiro \
  MODEL=claude-opus-5 \
  KIRO_JUDGE_MODEL=gpt-5.6-sol \
  scripts/run_task.sh tasks/<slug>

# agent on Bedrock, judge on Anthropic subscription
CC_MODE=bedrock JUDGE_MODE=anthropic \
  MODEL=claude-opus-5 JUDGE_MODEL=claude-sonnet-5 \
  ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-api03-... \
  scripts/run_task.sh tasks/<slug>

# agent on Bedrock, judge on OpenAI
CC_MODE=bedrock JUDGE_MODE=openai \
  MODEL=claude-opus-5 JUDGE_MODEL=gpt-5-turbo \
  OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... \
  scripts/run_task.sh tasks/<slug>
```

`JUDGE_MODE` is only honored when `CC_MODE=bedrock`. Unknown values are rejected with `JUDGE_MODE ERROR: unknown value 'X' (expected: bedrock | anthropic | openai | kiro)` and `exit 4` before the agent starts.

### `CC_MODE=kiro`

Both agent and judge talk to kiro-cli through a local two-key bridge. Agent and judge models are set independently per run.

```
scripts/run_task.sh starts kiro_bridge on 127.0.0.1:<ephemeral>
                           ├─ agent_key  pinned to  KIRO_MODEL        → kiro-cli
                           └─ judge_key  pinned to  KIRO_JUDGE_MODEL  → kiro-cli
```

- **Agent** (OpenHands container): `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://host:<port>` + `agent_key` → every tool call hits kiro-cli as `KIRO_MODEL`.
- **Judge** (verifier container): injected via Harbor `--ve` flags — `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=<judge_key>`, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://host:<port>`, `JUDGE_WIRE=anthropic`, `JUDGE_MODEL=<KIRO_JUDGE_MODEL>` (prevents the bundle's `rubric_judge_cli.py` from falling back to its hardcoded `claude-sonnet-5` default).
- **Prereq**: `kiro login` already done on the host; the bridge drives the host's logged-in CLI and holds no credentials of its own.

```bash
CC_MODE=kiro \
  KIRO_MODEL=claude-opus-5 \
  KIRO_JUDGE_MODEL=gpt-5.6-sol \
  scripts/run_task.sh tasks/<slug>
```

Omit `KIRO_JUDGE_MODEL` and the judge falls back to the agent model. The bridge mints a fresh `agent_key` and `judge_key` per run and tears both down at exit.

## Make targets

| Target | What it does |
|---|---|
| `make run-docker` | run agent-environment container on port 1984 |
| `make build` | build agent-environment locally |
| `make shell` | shell into agent-environment |
| `make install-harness` | install harness deps |
| `make run-harness` | run the TS harness on port 3001 (uses .env in cwd) |
| `make install-python` | install all Python deps (run_eval, scoring, diagnostics, test_servers) |
| `make run-eval` | run the full HuggingFace eval (usage: make run-eval MODEL=... OUTPUT=...) |
| `make test` | verify mcp_server_template.json and install_mcp_packages.sh stay in sync |
| `make build-openhands-runtime` | the OpenHands SDK tree the agent mounts; run_task.sh preflight builds it too |
| `make build-headroom-compress` | the agent-path Headroom proxy (AGENT_HEADROOM_ENABLED=true); preflight builds it too |
| `make install-harbor` | the pinned harbor, hash-checked (scripts/lib/harbor.sh) |
| `make ccbridge-check` | does this machine's Claude login load and refresh? spends no tokens |
| `make test-ccbridge` | the ccbridge's own unit tests |

## Layout

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `pyproject.toml` | the registered entry points and the pinned harbor; uv.lock beside it |
| `tools/cli.py` | harness-infer and harness-eval |
| `scripts/run_task.sh` | one task end to end: preflight, harbor, reshape, finance, mask |
| `scripts/run_batch.py` | every task x every attempt through run_task.sh's stages, checkpointed |
| `scripts/lib/harbor.sh` | the harbor pin and its hash-checked install |
| `scripts/lib/harbor-requirements.lock` | harbor's whole dependency closure, with hashes |
| `scripts/patch_harbor.py` | the edits made to the pinned harbor, each one or a loud refusal |
| `scripts/checkpoint.py` | the batch checkpoint run_batch.py resumes from |
| `scripts/stop_harness.sh` | stop the harness's bridges and sweep orphaned trial containers |
| `scripts/gen_readme.py` | this README |
| `tools/openhands_agent/` | the default agent under test: OpenHands behind harbor's agent interface |
| `tools/bridges/` | host-side model routes: ccbridge (Claude subscription), zbridge (GLM) |
| `tools/headroom/` | optional agent-path prompt compression (AGENT_HEADROOM_ENABLED) |
| `tools/network/` | network preflight against harbor's resolver, egress guard hook, internet audit |
| `tools/delivery_utils/` | reshape harbor's job dir into the per-task output tree; package deliveries |
| `tools/finance/` | usage reporting to Odoo after a run |
| `services/` | the upstream MCP-Atlas REST pipeline (agent-environment, agent-harness, mcp_eval, diagnostics, legacy scoring) |

## Tests

```bash
uv run --no-project --with pytest --with pyyaml python -m pytest scripts/tests
```

Tests that need Docker, an installed harbor, or credentials skip themselves when those are absent. `scripts/tests/test_readme.py` fails when this file is stale.
